title: chant workspace records output
description: What `chant workspace records --json` prints, version 1 of the read contract for records (#2536). This is the first-test slice (#2546): records are unsealed and there is no workspace declaration yet. Readers ignore fields they do not know; a field is only ever added within a version. The reason and error codes are closed lists: a new code is a new contract version. Contract version 1 is written by chant 0.81.0 and newer; a reader that needs it refuses output whose `contract` it doesn't know. Every code is in the one closed list of `reason-codes.ts`.

result.description: The read worked. Exit code 0, even when some records are invalid.

schema.description: The `$id` of the schema each record was validated against.

file.description: The kind file, relative to the repository root, with / separators.

at.description: The full commit id the records were read at (--at), or null for the working tree.

workspaceRoot.description: Added in contract 1 by #2549. The directory a record's pinned paths resolve in, from the repository root with / separators: the workspace whose declaration sits nearest above the kind file, or "." for the repository root.

current.description: Whether superseded records were left out (--current).

records.description: One entry per file the kind locates, sorted by path.

superseded.description: Records a closed record supersedes, counted before --current leaves them out.

id.description: Null when the front matter could not be parsed or has no string id.

path.description: From the repository root, with / separators.

state.description: The state as the record writes it. Supersession is reported in supersededBy, not here.

valid.description: True exactly when reasons is empty.

supersededBy.description: The id of the closed record whose supersedes link replaces this one. Derived from that record's link, never from this record's own fields.

data.description: The front matter as JSON, following the kind's schema when valid is true. Null when it could not be parsed.

assets.description: Added in contract 1 by #2549. Each workspace file the record pins by hash, checked against the tree read: the working tree, or the revision under --at. Empty for a kind that pins nothing.

warnings.description: Added in contract 1 by #2549. Findings that leave the record valid: a pinned file that changed, went missing or did not follow a superseding decision, or a supersedes link that has no effect yet. valid and --current do not look at them.

path.description: From the workspace root (workspaceRoot), with / separators.

actual.description: The hash of the file's bytes in the tree read, or null when the file is missing.

state.description: pinned when the hashes match; drifted when they differ (a warning asset-drift); missing when the file is not there (a warning asset-missing); stale when the hashes match and a record this one supersedes pinned the same hash, with the file unchanged since this record was recorded (a warning asset-stale).

trust.description: Added in contract 1 by #2547. Where provenance was judged from: the policy read at the base revision, never the tree read.

base.description: The full commit id the policy was read at, or null when there is no base.

baseFrom.description: flag when --base was given; otherwise the target branch that was found.

active.description: Whether a signers file exists at base. False means attestation is off and every record is unattested.

signersPath.description: The signers file, relative to the repository root.

problems.description: Why the policy could not be read. Nothing is attested when this is not empty.

provenance.description: Added in contract 1 by #2547. How far the record's authorship is established, judged by the signers at base.

level.description: attested: the last commit to change the file is signed by a signer the policy at base lists. attested-unverifiable-here: it carries a signature nothing here can check. adopted: it lies in a commit range the policy adopts. unattested: none of these, including uncommitted content.

commit.description: The commit the record's content comes from, or null for uncommitted content.

attestor.description: The attestor that answered, such as ssh-commit.

key.description: The signing key's fingerprint, when known.

failure.description: The read failed and returned no records. Exit code 1.
